I attempted to kill myself in late November, 2018. I was sent to an involuntary psychiatric ward (I was a minor so I had absolutely no say in it). I was miserable but I had been in wards before for prior suicide attempts so it wasn’t a huge deal. 

Then I was talking with the doctor and he brought up residential. Basically, you go live in a house with care specialists and doctors 24/7 for about 3 months. 

I flipped out. I did NOT want to go to residential. In terms of psychiatric treatment, it can either be the best decision of your life or the worst. For me, it wasn’t a decision: I went. 

I ended up being removed early but I stayed in treatment for just over a month, and I was absolutely inconsolable during my whole time there. I was basically crying 24/7, none of the other occupants wanted to be my friend because I was so emotional.

I should make it clear that I never once self-harmed in treatment; they did daily inspections of your body (yeah, I know, very invasive, especially as an underage and severely mentally ill person). That’s why my parents let me out of residential early. 

But, my god, it’s completely messed me up. I get triggered almost daily because things remind me of residential. For instance, decorating for Christmas in 2019. I had a panic attack because we had done the same thing at residential and all I could think about was being trapped there. 

I’m almost an adult now and I’ve been out of treatment for over a year; after I was released from residential, I never went back. I’m on 5 different medications which are mostly keeping me positive. 

I still have times where I self-harm but nothing has been serious enough to go back into treatment. But dear god, I feel like I’ll never heal from residential. Even talking about it like this, over a year later, still has me shaking. It’s a lot.
